AdvancedAnalysisFlow(Flow[MarketState]):\n    @start()\n    def fetch_market_data(self):\n        # Demonstrate low-level control with structured state\n        self.state.sentiment = \u0026quot;analyzing\u0026quot;\n        return {\u0026quot;sector\u0026quot;: \u0026quot;tech\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;timeframe\u0026quot;: \u0026quot;1W\u0026quot;}  # These parameters match the task description template\n\n    @listen(fetch_market_data)\n    def analyze_with_crew(self, market_data):\n        # Show crew agency through specialized roles\n        analyst = Agent(\n            role=\u0026quot;Senior Market Analyst\u0026quot;,\n            goal=\u0026quot;Conduct deep market analysis with expert insight\u0026quot;,\n            backstory=\u0026quot;You're a veteran analyst known for identifying subtle market patterns\u0026quot;\n        )\n        researcher = Agent(\n            role=\u0026quot;Data Researcher\u0026quot;,\n            goal=\u0026quot;Gather and validate supporting market data\u0026quot;,\n            backstory=\u0026quot;You excel at finding and correlating multiple data sources\u0026quot;\n        )\n\n        analysis_task = Task(\n            description=\u0026quot;Analyze {sector} sector data for the past {timeframe}\u0026quot;,\n            expected_output=\u0026quot;Detailed market analysis with confidence score\u0026quot;,\n            agent=analyst\n        )\n        research_task = Task(\n            description=\u0026quot;Find supporting data to validate the analysis\u0026quot;,\n            expected_output=\u0026quot;Corroborating evidence and potential contradictions\u0026quot;,\n            agent=researcher\n        )\n\n        # Demonstrate crew autonomy\n        analysis_crew = Crew(\n            agents=[analyst, researcher],\n            tasks=[analysis_task, research_task],\n            process=Process.sequential,\n            verbose=True\n        )\n        return analysis_crew.kickoff(inputs=market_data)  # Pass market_data as named inputs\n\n    @router(analyze_with_crew)\n    def determine_next_steps(self):\n        # Show flow control with conditional routing\n        if self.state.confidence \u0026gt; 0.8:\n            return \u0026quot;high_confidence\u0026quot;\n        elif self.state.confidence \u0026gt; 0.5:\n            return \u0026quot;medium_confidence\u0026quot;\n        return \u0026quot;low_confidence\u0026quot;\n\n    @listen(\u0026quot;high_confidence\u0026quot;)\n    def execute_strategy(self):\n        # Demonstrate complex decision making\n        strategy_crew = Crew(\n            agents=[\n                Agent(role=\u0026quot;Strategy Expert\u0026quot;,\n                      goal=\u0026quot;Develop optimal market strategy\u0026quot;)\n            ],\n            tasks=[\n                Task(description=\u0026quot;Create detailed strategy based on analysis\u0026quot;,\n                     expected_output=\u0026quot;Step-by-step action plan\u0026quot;)\n            ]\n        )\n        return strategy_crew.kickoff()\n\n    @listen(or_(\u0026quot;medium_confidence\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;low_confidence\u0026quot;))\n    def request_additional_analysis(self):\n        self.state.recommendations.append(\u0026quot;Gather improve the library by focusing our efforts on the most used features, integrations and tools.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt's pivotal to understand that \u003cstrong\u003eNO data is collected\u003c/strong\u003e concerning prompts, task descriptions, agents' backstories or goals, usage of tools, API calls, responses, any data processed by the agents, or secrets and environment variables, with the exception of the conditions mentioned. When the \u003ccode\u003eshare_crew\u003c/code\u003e feature is enabled, detailed data including task descriptions, agents' backstories or goals, and other specific attributes are collected to provide deeper insights while respecting user privacy. Users can disable telemetry by setting the environment variable OTEL_SDK_DISABLED to true.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eData collected includes:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eVersion of CrewAI\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSo we can understand how many users are using the latest version\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eVersion of Python\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSo we can decide on what versions to better support\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eGeneral OS (e.g. number of CPUs, macOS/Windows/Linux)\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSo we know what OS we should focus on and if we could build specific OS related features\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eNumber of agents and tasks in a crew\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSo we make sure we are testing internally with similar use cases and educate people on the best practices\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eCrew Process being used\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUnderstand where we should focus our efforts\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIf Agents are using memory or allowing delegation\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUnderstand if we improved the features or maybe even drop them\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIf Tasks are being executed in parallel or sequentially\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUnderstand if we should focus more on parallel execution\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eLanguage model being used\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eImproved support on most used languages\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRoles of agents in a crew\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUnderstand high level use cases so we can build better tools, integrations and examples about it\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eTools names available\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUnderstand out of the publicly available tools, which ones are being used the most so we can improve them\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eUsers can opt-in to Further Telemetry, sharing the complete telemetry data by setting the \u003ccode\u003eshare_crew\u003c/code\u003e attribute to \u003ccode\u003eTrue\u003c/code\u003e on their Crews. Enabling \u003ccode\u003eshare_crew\u003c/code\u003e results in the collection of detailed crew and task execution data, including \u003ccode\u003egoal\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebackstory\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003econtext\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eoutput\u003c/code\u003e of tasks. This enables a deeper insight into usage patterns while respecting the user's choice to share.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Fast and Flexible Multi-Agent Automation Framework</h3><a id="user-content-fast-and-flexible-multi-agent-automation-framework" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Fast and Flexible Multi-Agent Automation Framework" href="#fast-and-flexible-multi-agent-automation-framework"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">CrewAI is an open-source Python framework with high-level abstractions and low-level APIs for building production-ready multi-agent workflows.
It gives developers autonomous agent collaboration through Crews and precise, event-driven control through Flows.</p>
</blockquote>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>CrewAI Crews</strong>: Optimize for autonomy and collaborative intelligence with role-based AI agents.</li>
<li><strong>CrewAI Flows</strong>: Build event-driven automations that combine precise workflow control, single LLM calls, and native support for Crews.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">With over 100,000 developers certified through our community courses at <a href="https://learn.crewai.com" rel="nofollow">learn.crewai.com</a>, CrewAI is rapidly becoming the
standard for production-ready agentic automation.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">CrewAI AMP Suite</h1><a id="user-content-crewai-amp-suite" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: CrewAI AMP Suite" href="#crewai-amp-suite"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">For organizations that need a commercial control plane around CrewAI, <a href="https://crewai.com/amp" rel="nofollow">CrewAI AMP Suite</a> adds managed deployment, observability, governance, security, and enterprise support.</p>
<p dir="auto">You can try one part of the suite, the <a href="https://app.crewai.com" rel="nofollow">Crew Control Plane, for free</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Crew Control Plane Key Features:</h2><a id="user-content-crew-control-plane-key-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Crew Control Plane Key Features:" href="#crew-control-plane-key-features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Tracing & Observability</strong>: Monitor and track your AI agents and workflows in real-time, including metrics, logs, and traces.</li>
<li><strong>Unified Control Plane</strong>: A centralized platform for managing, monitoring, and scaling your AI agents and workflows.</li>
<li><strong>Seamless Integrations</strong>: Easily connect with existing enterprise systems, data sources, and cloud infrastructure.</li>
<li><strong>Advanced Security</strong>: Built-in robust security and compliance measures ensuring safe deployment and management.</li>
<li><strong>Actionable Insights</strong>: Real-time analytics and reporting to optimize performance and decision-making.</li>
<li><strong>24/7 Support</strong>: Dedicated enterprise support to ensure uninterrupted operation and quick resolution of issues.</li>
<li><strong>On-premise and Cloud Deployment Options</strong>: Deploy CrewAI AMP on-premise or in the cloud, depending on your security and compliance requirements.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">CrewAI AMP is designed for enterprises seeking a powerful, reliable solution to transform complex business processes into efficient,
intelligent automations.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Build with AI</h2><a id="user-content-build-with-ai" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Build with AI" href="#build-with-ai"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Using an AI coding agent? Teach it CrewAI best practices in one command:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Claude Code:</strong></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="/plugin marketplace add crewAIInc/skills
/plugin install crewai-skills@crewai-plugins
/reload-plugins"><pre>/plugin marketplace add crewAIInc/skills
/plugin install crewai-skills@crewai-plugins
/reload-plugins</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Four skills that activate automatically when you ask relevant CrewAI questions:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Skill</th>
<th>When it runs</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>getting-started</code></td>
<td>Scaffolding new projects, choosing between <code>LLM.call()</code> / <code>Agent</code> / <code>Crew</code> / <code>Flow</code>, wiring <code>crew.py</code> / <code>main.py</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>design-agent</code></td>
<td>Configuring agents — role, goal, backstory, tools, LLMs, memory, guardrails</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>design-task</code></td>
<td>Writing task descriptions, dependencies, structured output (<code>output_pydantic</code>, <code>output_json</code>), human review</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ask-docs</code></td>
<td>Querying the live <a href="https://docs.crewai.com/mcp" rel="nofollow">CrewAI docs MCP server</a> for up-to-date API details</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and others (<a href="https://skills.sh/crewaiinc/skills" rel="nofollow">skills.sh</a>):</strong></p>

<p dir="auto">This installs the official <a href="https://github.com/crewAIInc/skills">CrewAI Skills</a> — structured instructions that teach coding agents how to scaffold Flows, configure Crews, design agents and tasks, and follow CrewAI patterns.</p>

<p dir="auto">CrewAI unlocks the true potential of multi-agent automation, delivering speed, flexibility, and control through Crews of AI agents and event-driven Flows:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Purpose-built architecture</strong>: Designed specifically for agent orchestration, with a lightweight Python core and clean primitives for real-world automation.</li>
<li><strong>High Performance</strong>: Optimized for speed and minimal resource usage, enabling faster execution.</li>
<li><strong>Flexible Low-Level Customization</strong>: Complete freedom to customize everything from workflows and system architecture to agent behaviors, internal prompts, and execution logic.</li>
<li><strong>Ideal for Every Use Case</strong>: Proven effective for simple tasks, complex workflows, and production-grade automation.</li>
<li><strong>Robust Community</strong>: Backed by a rapidly growing community of over <strong>100,000 certified</strong> developers offering comprehensive support and resources.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">CrewAI empowers developers and teams to build intelligent automations that balance simplicity, flexibility, and production-grade control.</p>

<p dir="auto">CrewAI offers two powerful, complementary approaches that work seamlessly together to build sophisticated AI applications:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Crews</strong>: Teams of AI agents with true autonomy and agency, working together to accomplish complex tasks through role-based collaboration. Crews enable:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Natural, autonomous decision-making between agents</li>
<li>Dynamic task delegation and collaboration</li>
<li>Specialized roles with defined goals and expertise</li>
<li>Flexible problem-solving approaches</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Flows</strong>: Production-ready, event-driven workflows that deliver precise control over complex automations. Flows provide:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Fine-grained control over execution paths for real-world scenarios</li>
<li>Secure, consistent state management between tasks</li>
<li>Clean integration of AI agents with production Python code</li>
<li>Conditional branching for complex business logic</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">The true power of CrewAI emerges when combining Crews and Flows. This synergy allows you to:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Build complex, production-grade applications</li>
<li>Balance autonomy with precise control</li>
<li>Handle sophisticated real-world scenarios</li>
<li>Maintain clean, maintainable code structure</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">To get started with CrewAI, follow these simple steps:</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">1. Installation</h3><a id="user-content-1-installation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 1. Installation" href="#1-installation"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Ensure you have Python >=3.10 <3.14 installed on your system. CrewAI uses <a href="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/" rel="nofollow">UV</a> for dependency management and package handling, offering a seamless setup and execution experience.</p>
<p dir="auto">First, install CrewAI:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="uv pip install crewai"><pre>uv pip install crewai</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">If you want to install the 'crewai' package along with its optional features that include additional tools for agents, you can do so by using the following command:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="uv pip install 'crewai[tools]'"><pre>uv pip install <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>crewai[tools]<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The command above installs the basic package and also adds extra components which require more dependencies to function.</p>

<p dir="auto">If you encounter issues during installation or usage, here are some common solutions:</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Common Issues</h4><a id="user-content-common-issues" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Common Issues" href="#common-issues"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tiktoken'</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Install tiktoken explicitly: <code>uv pip install 'crewai[embeddings]'</code></li>
<li>If using embedchain or other tools: <code>uv pip install 'crewai[tools]'</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Failed building wheel for tiktoken</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">

<li>Try upgrading pip: <code>uv pip install --upgrade pip</code></li>

</ul>
</li>

<p dir="auto">To create a new CrewAI project, run the following CLI (Command Line Interface) command:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="crewai create crew <project_name>"><pre>crewai create crew <span class="pl-k"><</span>project_name<span class="pl-k">></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This command creates a new project folder with the following structure:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="my_project/
├── .gitignore
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
├── .env
└── src/
    └── my_project/
        ├── __init__.py
        ├── main.py
        ├── crew.py
        ├── tools/
        │   ├── custom_tool.py
        │   └── __init__.py
        └── config/
            ├── agents.yaml
            └── tasks.yaml"><pre class="notranslate"><code>my_project/
├── .gitignore
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
├── .env
└── src/
    └── my_project/
        ├── __init__.py
        ├── main.py
        ├── crew.py

        │   └── __init__.py
        └── config/
            ├── agents.yaml
            └── tasks.yaml
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">You can now start developing your crew by editing the files in the <code>src/my_project</code> folder. The <code>main.py</code> file is the entry point of the project, the <code>crew.py</code> file is where you define your crew, the <code>agents.yaml</code> file is where you define your agents, and the <code>tasks.yaml</code> file is where you define your tasks.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">To customize your project, you can:</h4><a id="user-content-to-customize-your-project-you-can" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: To customize your project, you can:" href="#to-customize-your-project-you-can"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Modify <code>src/my_project/config/agents.yaml</code> to define your agents.</li>
<li>Modify <code>src/my_project/config/tasks.yaml</code> to define your tasks.</li>
<li>Modify <code>src/my_project/crew.py</code> to add your own logic, tools, and specific arguments.</li>
<li>Modify <code>src/my_project/main.py</code> to add custom inputs for your agents and tasks.</li>
<li>Add your environment variables into the <code>.env</code> file.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Instantiate your crew:</p>

	"""LatestAiDevelopment crew"""
	agents: List[BaseAgent]
	tasks: List[Task]

	@agent
	def researcher(self) -> Agent:
		return Agent(
			config=self.agents_config['researcher'],
			verbose=True,
			tools=[SerperDevTool()]
		)

	@agent
	def reporting_analyst(self) -> Agent:
		return Agent(
			config=self.agents_config['reporting_analyst'],
			verbose=True
		)

	@task
	def research_task(self) -> Task:
		return Task(
			config=self.tasks_config['research_task'],
		)

	@task
	def reporting_task(self) -> Task:
		return Task(
			config=self.tasks_config['reporting_task'],
			output_file='report.md'
		)

	@crew

		"""Creates the LatestAiDevelopment crew"""
		return Crew(

<p dir="auto">Before running your crew, make sure you have the following keys set as environment variables in your <code>.env</code> file:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>An <a href="https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys" rel="nofollow">OpenAI API key</a> (or other LLM API key): <code>OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...</code></li>
<li>A <a href="https://serper.dev/" rel="nofollow">Serper.dev</a> API key: <code>SERPER_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY_HERE</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Lock the dependencies and install them by using the CLI command but first, navigate to your project directory:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cd my_project
crewai install (Optional)"><pre><span class="pl-c1">cd</span> my_project
crewai install (Optional)</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">To run your crew, execute the following command in the root of your project:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="crewai run"><pre>crewai run</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">or</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="python src/my_project/main.py"><pre>python src/my_project/main.py</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">If an error happens due to the usage of poetry, please run the following command to update your crewai package:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="crewai update"><pre>crewai update</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">You should see the output in the console and the <code>report.md</code> file should be created in the root of your project with the full final report.</p>
<p dir="auto">In addition to the sequential process, you can use the hierarchical process, which automatically assigns a manager to the defined crew to properly coordinate the planning and execution of tasks through delegation and validation of results. <a href="https://docs.crewai.com/en/concepts/processes" rel="nofollow">See more about the processes here</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Key Features</h2><a id="user-content-key-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Key Features" href="#key-features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">CrewAI gives developers a practical foundation for building agentic systems that move from prototype to production: autonomous collaboration where it helps, explicit workflow control where it matters, and Python-native customization throughout.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Crews for autonomy</strong>: Model teams of specialized AI agents with roles, goals, tools, and tasks.</li>
<li><strong>Flows for control</strong>: Build event-driven workflows with state, branching, routing, and production logic.</li>
<li><strong>Seamless integration</strong>: Combine Crews and Flows to create complex, real-world automations.</li>
<li><strong>Python-native customization</strong>: Customize prompts, tools, execution paths, state, and integrations without fighting the framework.</li>
<li><strong>Agent-ready capabilities</strong>: Use tools, memory, knowledge, checkpointing, async execution, and MCP/A2A support for more capable production agents.</li>
<li><strong>Production-ready patterns</strong>: Add deterministic steps, human input, structured outputs, and checkpointing as your system grows.</li>
<li><strong>Thriving community</strong>: Backed by robust documentation and over 100,000 certified developers, providing exceptional support and guidance.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Choose CrewAI to build powerful, adaptable, and production-ready AI automations.</p>

<p dir="auto">CrewAI's power truly shines when combining Crews with Flows to create sophisticated automation pipelines.
CrewAI flows support logical operators like <code>or_</code> and <code>and_</code> to combine multiple conditions. This can be used with <code>@start</code>, <code>@listen</code>, or <code>@router</code> decorators to create complex triggering conditions.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>or_</code>: Triggers when any of the specified conditions are met.</li>
<li><code>and_</code>: Triggers when all of the specified conditions are met.</li>
</ul>

        researcher = Agent(

            tasks=[analysis_task, research_task],

            verbose=True
        )

<p dir="auto">CrewAI supports using various LLMs through a variety of connection options. By default your agents will use the OpenAI API when querying the model. However, there are several other ways to allow your agents to connect to models. For example, you can configure your agents to use a local model via the Ollama tool.</p>
<p dir="auto">Please refer to the <a href="https://docs.crewai.com/en/learn/llm-connections" rel="nofollow">Connect CrewAI to LLMs</a> page for details on configuring your agents' connections to models.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">When to Use CrewAI</h2><a id="user-content-when-to-use-crewai" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: When to Use CrewAI" href="#when-to-use-crewai"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Use CrewAI when you need more than a single prompt or chatbot: multi-step work, specialized agents, tool use, structured outputs, human review, or workflows that combine autonomous reasoning with explicit business logic.</p>
<p dir="auto">CrewAI is especially useful when you want to:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Coordinate multiple agents with clear roles and tasks.</li>
<li>Wrap agent work in deterministic, event-driven workflows.</li>
<li>Keep application logic in regular Python.</li>
<li>Move from experiment to production without changing frameworks.</li>
<li>Add tools, memory, checkpointing, and async execution as your system grows.</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Telemetry</h2><a id="user-content-telemetry" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Telemetry" href="#telemetry"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">CrewAI uses anonymous telemetry to collect usage data with the main purpose of helping us improve the library by focusing our efforts on the most used features, integrations and tools.</p>
<p dir="auto">It's pivotal to understand that <strong>NO data is collected</strong> concerning prompts, task descriptions, agents' backstories or goals, usage of tools, API calls, responses, any data processed by the agents, or secrets and environment variables, with the exception of the conditions mentioned. When the <code>share_crew</code> feature is enabled, detailed data including task descriptions, agents' backstories or goals, and other specific attributes are collected to provide deeper insights while respecting user privacy. Users can disable telemetry by setting the environment variable OTEL_SDK_DISABLED to true.</p>
<p dir="auto">Data collected includes:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Version of CrewAI
<ul dir="auto">
<li>So we can understand how many users are using the latest version</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Version of Python
<ul dir="auto">
<li>So we can decide on what versions to better support</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>General OS (e.g. number of CPUs, macOS/Windows/Linux)
<ul dir="auto">
<li>So we know what OS we should focus on and if we could build specific OS related features</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Number of agents and tasks in a crew
<ul dir="auto">
<li>So we make sure we are testing internally with similar use cases and educate people on the best practices</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Crew Process being used
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Understand where we should focus our efforts</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If Agents are using memory or allowing delegation
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Understand if we improved the features or maybe even drop them</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If Tasks are being executed in parallel or sequentially
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Understand if we should focus more on parallel execution</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Language model being used
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Improved support on most used languages</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Roles of agents in a crew
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Understand high level use cases so we can build better tools, integrations and examples about it</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Tools names available
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Understand out of the publicly available tools, which ones are being used the most so we can improve them</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Users can opt-in to Further Telemetry, sharing the complete telemetry data by setting the <code>share_crew</code> attribute to <code>True</code> on their Crews. Enabling <code>share_crew</code> results in the collection of detailed crew and task execution data, including <code>goal</code>, <code>backstory</code>, <code>context</code>, and <code>output</code> of tasks. This enables a deeper insight into usage patterns while respecting the user's choice to share.</p>
